subject: DPA & Subprocessors: TOMs exhibit and signature coordination
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Emma White <emma.white@acme-corp.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2026-06-12 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Initial DPA for review + TOMs exhibit

Hi Emma,

Thanks again for the productive call this morning. Per our discussion, attaching a working DPA (DPA_v3_redlines.pdf) and the current TOMs exhibit for Acme-specific handling. High-level items we flagged that I think we should resolve before signature:

- Subprocessors: Acme asked for a full list; we are proposing a managed-subprocessor list in Appendix A and an update notification process (30 days).
- Data transfers: we include SCCs but Acme prefers explicit EU controller-to-processor language; happy to confirm the EU addendum.
- Key management: Acme asked whether BYOK is supported; short answer is we support customer-managed keys in our Private offering but for Hosted API we offer envelope encryption + HSM-backed keys.
- TOMs: proposed edits around encryption-at-rest detail, RBAC/least-privilege, and quarterly access reviews.

Please review and let me know the must-haves vs. nice-to-haves. If acceptable, we'll route for legal + security review and send for signature via DocuSign.

Thanks,
Rishi
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0183

Attachments: DPA_v3_redlines.pdf, TOMs_exhibit_edited.docx

From: Emma White <emma.white@acme-corp.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: olivia.jackson@acme-corp.com
Date: 2026-06-12 13:48:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Initial DPA for review + TOMs exhibit

Rishi,

Thanks — quick notes inline:

- Subprocessors: we need a commitment that Acme will be notified at least 45 days before onboarding any subprocessor that will process Acme personal data, and the right to object in writing within 20 days for high-risk processors.
- Data transfers: we require the SCCs to be explicitly incorporated and a fallback statement about future adequacy decisions.
- Encryption/Key mgmt: Acme's procurement requires a BYOK capability or, alternatively, a written attestation that keys are isolated per-tenant and backed by a FIPS-certified HSM. Can you confirm which option you can commit to for the hosted environment?

We can live with a 30-day subprocessor notice if you provide a scope-limiting objection right for processors that handle identity data.

If you can make those changes, we can escalate internally to legal and aim to sign this week.

Best,
Emma
Head of Procurement, Acme Corp
emma.white@acme-corp.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-06-13 08:05:00 -0400
Subject: Fwd: Acme feedback on DPA / TOMs — need legal + security input

Folks,

Forwarding Acme's responses. Key asks that need a short position and (if possible) a clean redline:

1) Subprocessor notice window: Acme requests 45 days + 20-day objection window for high-risk processors. We typically do 30 days + objection right for processors handling sensitive data. Can legal confirm a stance?
2) BYOK or HSM attestation for hosted: security, is it feasible to provide a tenant-isolated HSM attestation for hosted customers, or do we need to limit BYOK to Private deployments only?
3) SCCs + fallback language: legal, we should confirm wording for EU transfers.

Attachments: DPA_v3_redlines.pdf (original), TOMs_exhibit_edited.docx

Thanks — Rishi

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-14 11:22:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Fwd: Acme feedback on DPA / TOMs — need legal + security input

Rishi / team,

Quick legal read and proposed positions to keep momentum:

- Subprocessors: push back to 30-day notice with a 15-day objection window limited to processors that will have access to "personal identifiers" or authentication data. This preserves our operational cadence while giving Acme a narrow exclusion right.
- SCCs: include standard EU SCC attachment and add a clause referencing future adequacy decisions; we'll add language that SCCs govern until replaced by an adequacy decision.
- BYOK/HSM: we should avoid committing BYOK for Hosted. Proposed compromise: provide a written attestation that keys are tenant-isolated, encrypted with HSM-backed master keys (FIPS 140-2 level 3 where applicable), and offer Private deployment or dedicated HSM for full BYOK.
- TOMs exhibit: I've edited the exhibit to add explicit items: encryption-in-transit (TLS 1.2+), encryption-at-rest algorithms (AES-256), role-based access control matrix, quarterly access review cadence, and key rotation policy summary. See TOMs_exhibit_edited.docx.

I suggest Grace shepherd the customer communications and send a single DocuSign envelope with the DPA + TOMs exhibit attached once security signs off. Vivek — are you comfortable with the attestation language above? If not, flag the specific sentences that need adjustment.

Monica
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Emma White <emma.white@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-15 17:45:00 -0400
Subject: Final DPA + TOMs exhibit — attestation and DocuSign

Emma,

Thanks for the rapid review and the clear asks. We've incorporated a compromise that should address Acme's concerns while keeping our Hosted offering practical:

- Subprocessors: 30-day notification and a 15-day objection window limited to processors that will have access to "personal identifiers" or authentication data. We will include a rolling Appendix A with current subprocessors and a commitment to publish changes in advance.
- Data transfers: SCCs are included; we also add a clause that SCCs apply until an applicable adequacy decision replaces them.
- Encryption & Key mgmt: For Hosted customers we cannot offer full BYOK at this time. Instead, we provide the following attestation (excerpt): "Redwood uses tenant-isolated data encryption keys encrypted under HSM-protected master keys (FIPS 140-2 Level 3 where available). Access to master keys is restricted to a small ops team under strict RBAC with quarterly reviews and audit logging." We also offer Private deployment with BYOK when desired.
- TOMs: updated exhibit lists AES-256 at rest, TLS 1.2+ in transit, role-based access control, quarterly access reviews, and key rotation every 12 months (or upon suspected compromise).

If that aligns, I've prepared the final DPA with those edits and uploaded the package to DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/envelope/789123. Envelope includes DPA_v3_final.pdf and TOMs_exhibit_final.docx.

We can accept signature from a procurement delegate and legal. Let me know if you want a short call to walk through the attestation language. Otherwise we'll initiate the DocuSign envelope and target signature by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.ai

DocuSign envelope: DocuSign_envelope_789123.link
